Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.
List has been revised.

2. Heard Shri Satyam Narayan holding brief of Shri Shashi Prakash Pandey , learned counsel for the applicant and other side not present as well as Shri Rajesh Kumar Srivastava, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

3. Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No. 22 of 2021, under Sections 366, 504, 506, 376 I.P.C.,
Police Station Salempur, District Bulandshahr during the pendency of trial.
4.
As per prosecution story, The applicant is stated to have enticed away the wife of the informant aged 25 years on 29.01.2021 at about 10.30 am.
When the informant went to the house of the applicant to complain the matter to his family members, they are stated to have threatened him and even asked him to refrain from filing any FIR or so.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that the applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
The fact that the victim had gone on the motorcycle along with the applicant with her infant on the way to Delhi.
There is an FIR No. 0022 of 2021 which was lodged by the father of applicant against one Pushpendra and others.
The informant is an employee of said accused Pushpendra, thus he has been falsely implicated in the case.
Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
There is no criminal history of the applicant.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 17.10.2022.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.
6. Per contra, learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the bail application but unable to dispute the submissions raised by the learned counsel for the applicant.

7. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, the fact of delay in lodging the FIR and the age of the victim and also there being a possibility of FIR being filed as counter-blast to FIR No. 0022 of 2021 and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

8. Let the applicant- Surendra Singh involved in aforementioned case crime number be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two heavy sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence during the trial.
(ii). The applicant will not pressurize/ intimidate the prosecution witness.
(iii) The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.
(iv) The applicant shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which he is accused, or suspected of the commission of which he is suspected.

(v) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
9.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
Identity, status and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the court concerned before the bonds are accepted.
